section_1.title: The Intuition: What is Information?
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of 'surprise' in data. Information is measured by how much a result narrows down the set of possibilities. We define 'Entropy' as the average amount of surprise or uncertainty reduction per guess.
section_1.example: Visual: A bag of 100 colored balls (99 white, 1 black). Finding the black ball provides high 'information' (low probability), while finding a white ball provides low 'information'.

section_2.title: Mathematical Foundation: Shannon Entropy
section_2.content: Define the formula H = -Σ p(i) log2 p(i). Explain that each guess in Wordle creates a 'partition' of possible remaining words. Entropy measures the spread of these partitions; we want a guess that splits the pool as evenly as possible.
section_2.example: Visual: A bar graph showing a 'flat' distribution (high entropy/better) vs. a 'spiked' distribution (low entropy/worse) when analyzing the impact of the word 'CRANE'.

section_3.title: Strategy: Maximizing Information Gain
section_3.content: Apply the theory to Wordle. A 'good' word isn't necessarily one that matches letters, but one that eliminates the largest number of incorrect candidates. Explain the transition from 'Maximum Entropy' (best average case) to 'Minimax' (best worst-case).
section_3.example: Scenario: 'CRANE' vs. 'XYLYL'. 'CRANE' eliminates thousands of words regardless of the feedback pattern, whereas 'XYLYL' rarely helps narrow the field.

section_4.title: Application: The Game Logic
section_4.content: Show the feedback loop: Guess -> Partition remaining word set -> Recalculate entropy for all remaining words -> Pick the highest entropy word. This is how algorithms like 'WordleBot' beat humans.
section_4.example: Animated flow: Robot character 'Bit' looks at the list of 2,309 possible words, simulates the 'grey', 'yellow', and 'green' outcomes, and selects the word with the highest entropy value.

section_5.title: Summary & Conclusion
section_5.content: Reiterate that entropy is a tool for decision-making under uncertainty. Mastery of information theory allows us to turn a game of 'guessing' into a game of 'optimization'.
section_5.example: Visual: A 'decision tree' shrinking from thousands of branches down to one single leaf node in just 3-4 steps.

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Shannon entropy formula defines information uncertainty.",
            "Guesses create partitions of the remaining words.",
            "Entropy measures how evenly we split partitions.",
            "Balanced splits maximize information gain.",
            "Uneven partitions represent low entropy."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Foundation: Shannon Entropy", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show Shannon Entropy formula: H(X) = -sum(p log p)
        formula = MathTex(r"H(X) = -\sum p(i) \log_2 p(i)", color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Explain variables p (probability) and H (entropy)
        label_h = Text("H = Uncertainty", font_size=24).next_to(formula, DOWN)
        label_p = Text("p = Probability", font_size=24).next_to(label_h, DOWN)
        self.play(Write(label_h), Write(label_p))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Visualize a probability distribution curve shifting
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 1, 0.5], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5, x_range=[0, 4])
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'D2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_in_area(curve, 'D2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF4500")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Show how entropy values change as distribution becomes uniform
        new_curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2 + 0.3 * np.exp(-(x-2)**2), x_range=[0, 4], color=BLUE)
        self.play(Transform(curve, new_curve))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00CED1")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Final summary: Entropy measures uncertainty in the system.
        summary = Text("Entropy = Uncertainty", font_size=30, color=RED).move_to(self.grid['F3'])
        self.play(FadeIn(summary))
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#DC143C")
        self.wait(2)

section_1.title: The Intuition: What is Information?
lecture_lines: Information is measured by narrowing down possibilities.
Surprise equates to the amount of information gained.
Entropy quantifies the average surprise of a result.
Finding rare outcomes yields high information.
Common outcomes provide little new information.

section_2.title: Mathematical Foundation: Shannon Entropy

Guesses create partitions of the remaining words.
Entropy measures how evenly we split partitions.
Balanced splits maximize information gain.
Uneven partitions represent low entropy.
